pr_title: In JS interop, handle ValueTask equivalently as Task (#40198)
pr_body:
# In JS interop, handle ValueTask equivalently as Task 

Add logic for handling async JSInvokable methods returning ValueType in DotnetDispatcher

## Description

Since we can't do pattern matching as was done with Task since ValueTask apparently doesn't have non generic type we can use here I had to do reflection check if asyncResult is of generic type ValueTask<>. Then I proceeded to get AsTask method allowing me to use the same flow as was used for Task.

Fixes #40198

issue_context.title: In JS interop, handle ValueTask equivalently as Task
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe the problem.

Currently, `[JSInvokable]` methods can be sync or async, but if they are async, they are limited to returning `Task`/`Task<T>`.

We don't currently allow `ValueTask`/`ValueTask<T>`. If a developer does in fact define a method like this:

```cs
[JSInvokable]
ValueTask<T> SomeMethod() { ... }
```

... then because there's no logic in JSInterop to recognize `ValueTask`/`ValueTask<T>`, we JSON-serialize the whole ValueTask and treat it as a synchronous result. As it happens, `ValueTask` JSON-serializes quite happily so there's no exception, but the result on the JS side is pretty useless.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I can't immediately think of any reason we shouldn't update `DotNetDispatcher.cs`'s `BeginInvokeDotNet` logic to recognize `ValueTask` and handle it in the same way we handle `Task`.

### Additional context

I think there are legit use cases for a JS-invokable method to want to return `ValueTask<T>`, e.g., when the method returns possibly-cached values, if the cache entry exists synchronously, it can do `ValueTask.FromResult(result)`.
